source_text: Ἐὰν δὲ φαγὼν φάγῃ ἀπὸ τῶν κρεῶν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ, οὐ δεχθήσεται αὐτῷ τῷ προσφέροντι αὐτὸ, οὐ λογισθήσεται αὐτῷ, μίασμά ἐστιν· ἡ δὲ ψυχὴ ἤτις ἂν φάγῃ ἀπ' αὐτοῦ, μιανθήσεται, καὶ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν λήψεται.» Τριταῖον μὲν οὖν ἀποπέμπεται θῦμα, παρα
pass_a_gloss: …tritē hēmera… miasma… skybala… Thysian ouk ēthelēsas… telos nomou Christos…
pass_b_english: Cyril: If eating he should eat from the meats on the third day, it will not be accepted for him who brings it forward, it will not be reckoned for him, it is a pollution; and the soul which should eat from it will be polluted, and will take the sin.’ So then a third-day victim is sent away, and he was clarifying that he also declines the yesterday’s saying. ‘And if you should sacrifice a sacrifice of a vow of gladness to the Lord, unto acceptable for you you will sacrifice it. On that very day it will be eaten, it will not be left from the meats unto the morning; I am Lord; he will take the sin.’ (Leviticus 7:18)
Palladius: Then what mind of these also would come to be?

Cyril: The law has shown beforehand for us in the things above very often, that it is custom for the divine Scripture to cut all time, sometimes unto two, according to which the law was, and according to which Christ has shone upon; and sometimes again, unto three with the chorus of the holy prophets also being brought in between and arranging the things, yet that also in time the according to Moses, and in that of the holy prophets, the manner of worship was the same, as still in shadows the according to law. And when morning has come to be—that is, when the third time has been shown again, and the intelligible light, that is, Christ, flashing around the under-sun, and with the ancient mist having been loosed—the manner of the worship then is no longer acceptable, but whether yesterday’s, or the third-day fat, or victim, is no longer acceptable, but abominable and rejectable beside God, and having been reckoned in an order of pollution for those who have chosen to bring forward not in season. Or do you not say it is true, that with Christ flashing upon the souls of the saints with the Gospel pedagogies and mystagoguing very well unto the spiritual worship, the things in law are somehow already superfluous and unbeneficial?

Palladius: I say. For I will remember all-divine Paul, who has called the boasts according to law dung and loss, through the surpassing of the knowledge of Christ. And I hear him having written to some: ‘And I say to you that if you should be circumcised, Christ will benefit us nothing.’ (Leviticus 19:5–8)

Cyril: You have spoken uprightly. So then it is sin and pollution, when Christ has been shown, and the time has driven past according to which the law and the prophets were, to hold against the worship as in shadows; and to attempt to bring forward to God a sheep, or fat, or frankincense; though the Son says clearly to God and Father: ‘Sacrifice and offering you did not will, but a body you fitted for me. Whole-burnt-offerings and concerning sin you were not well-pleased, then I said, Behold I have come; in a heading of a book it has been written concerning me, to do, O God, your will.’ (Philippians 3:8) For having dedicated himself as an unblemished victim for us, the Son has set the things in law, not able to take away sins; for end of law and of prophets is Christ (Galatians 5:2) (Hebrews 10:5–7) (Romans 10:4).
